prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1186; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by the third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Both vehicles were drivable from the scene. Claimant reports neck and back pain at the time of the loss and has since been seen at an urgent care clinic.

Entry 2: Received notice of representation. Claimant has retained counsel, and all further contact is to go through the attorney's office. Letter of representation acknowledged and placed in file. Diary set to follow up on the medical records request once the authorization is returned.

Entry 3: Liability review completed. The third-party driver admitted following too closely in the recorded statement. Photos of both vehicles show rear damage to the insured vehicle consistent with the reported impact. Liability is assessed as clear against the third-party insured. Property damage estimate is being prepared by the field appraiser.

Entry 4: Medical records received from the treating provider. Diagnosis is cervical and lumbar strain with muscle spasm. Treatment to date includes physical therapy, prescribed muscle relaxants, and a series of chiropractic visits. Treating physician notes the claimant's range of motion is improving but remains limited. No imaging showed fracture. Bodily injury evaluation pending receipt of the therapy discharge summary.

Entry 5: Spoke with claimant's counsel regarding the status of the bodily injury claim. Counsel has requested a demand package, which will include the medical bills, records, and wage documentation. Advised counsel that the property damage claim is moving forward separately. Reserves reviewed and adjusted to reflect the current treatment course. File remains open pending the demand.
